name: Berwang
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful mountain village in the upper Lechtal with one of the most stunning panoramas of the Lechtaler Alpen.
beschreibung:
Overview

Berwang is a picturesque mountain municipality in the Reutte district of the Tyrolean Außerfern region, perched at an altitude of approximately 1,336 meters. As the highest village in the entire Tiroler Zugspitz Arena, this alpine haven of roughly 600 residents is nestled on a sunny high mountain pass between the Berwang Valley and the Rotlech Valley. Directly above the village looms Mount Thaneller at 2,341 meters, renowned as one of the most magnificent panoramic summits in the Lechtal Alps. Free from through-traffic, Berwang seamlessly blends peaceful seclusion with ski-in/ski-out convenience in winter and serves as a premier summer retreat for hikers and mountain enthusiasts.

History

The village name derives from Middle High German ber (bear) and wang (meadow), literally translating to Bear's Meadow, an origin preserved today by an upright black bear depicted on the municipal coat of arms. Colonization began in the 12th century when the Lords of Starkenberg established cattle-farming homesteads from the Imst area. Around 1266, Count Meinhard II acquired the territory, incorporating it into the County of Tyrol, with jurisdiction later held by the court of Ehrenberg from 1430. For centuries, residents endured impoverished conditions as mountain farmers. In the 18th and 19th centuries, extreme poverty compelled many families to send their children as seasonal farm laborers (Schwabenkinder) to southern Germany. The parish church of Saint James the Elder features a Gothic choir dating to 1430 and a Baroque nave from the 18th century. A pioneer of alpine winter sports, Berwang hosted the very first ski course in the Außerfern back in 1914, followed in 1949 by its first tow lift, ushering in modern tourism.

How to Get There

By car, visitors can reach Berwang toll-free from Germany via motorway A7 through Füssen/Reutte or motorway A95 via Garmisch-Partenkirchen along the Fernpass federal highway B179 to Bichlbach, where provincial road L24 ascends four kilometers to Berwang. From the Inn Valley, access is via the Fernpass road. Train travelers take the Außerfern Railway to Bichlbach-Berwang station. From there, regular VVT buses on route 152 and free guest shuttles provide direct access into Berwang and Rinnen.

Tips

An ascent of Mount Thaneller rewards hikers with a sweeping 360-degree panorama extending from the Zugspitze massif to the Karwendel mountains. The family-friendly Berwang-Bichlbach ski area offers 36 kilometers of pistes and modern lift infrastructure, including the Obere Karbahn gondola on Thanellerkar, offering genuine ski-in/ski-out access from village chalets. In summer, the Bärenbad forest swimming pool at 1,336 meters treats guests to heated outdoor pools and recreation lawns. In the hamlet of Rinnen, the roaring Rotlech Waterfall and scenic Rotlech Reservoir showcase unspoiled natural majesty.
